scope: Read-only root-cause/design review plus standalone immutable-JSON reader tests. No product source modifications.

published_failure_reported_by_parent.error: HTTP 409 E_SOURCE_REVIEW Source ddg: Missing colon

root_cause: SourceSpec::require_review calls validate_contract, whose guard_shape and deep-clone path serialize the retained shared contract.
Json::dump calls json_object_to_json_string_ext and copies from the returned native buffer without synchronization.
Disassembly of the actual local json-c serializer shows read/creation/reset of per-object printbuf and return of its buffer pointer.

The local installed json-c 0.17-1build1 uses non-atomic read-modify-write in json_object_get/put; Json::at, copy, push/set and destruction therefore can race even for logically immutable registry trees.

upstream_primary_sources.observation: ENABLE_THREADING only makes get/put atomic, is disabled by default, and does not provide full concurrent tree access; key-hash initialization has a separate compare-and-swap path.

upstream_primary_sources.section: Object ownership, child lookup, serializer APIs
upstream_primary_sources.observation: Child lookup does not retain ownership; object/array add transfers it; put may release a tree recursively.

confirmed_shared_reader_paths: HTTP Store::search_submit -> normalized_request -> SourceSpec::require_review occurs before Store mutex.
Background Store::lease_next_search -> SourceSpec::require_review occurs while holding Store mutex; the other path is not covered by that mutex.
WebService::enabled_sources/sources/search also call reviewed/require_review on retained contracts.
Store::search_submit contracts.push and Store::freeze_search_locked contract.at("review") retain/read the same shared contract tree.
SiteSpec::require_review/approved field reads share SiteSpec.review across admission and site-description paths.
excluded_candidate: WebService search cache stores serialized std::string and parses new independent trees in cache_get; no shared cached Json node was found there.
minimum_design: One mutex shared across all json-c nodes/aliases, not a per-Json-wrapper or per-SourceSpec mutex.
Protect all native calls touching shared nodes and implicit retain/release: copy/get, destructor/put, lookup plus retain, get plus add/set, scalar reads, size, key iteration, dump and str.
Keep native returned buffer/string/key copying inside the mutex; no raw pointer escapes the critical section.
For a nonrecursive mutex, avoid acquiring it before calling other Json methods that acquire it. Pure local parser state can remain outside the lock when it cannot refer to published shared nodes.
Canonical may compose individually protected methods when the documented contract requires caller synchronization for concurrent mutation or multi-operation read/modify/write.

Use a process-lifetime mutex or prove initialization/destruction ordering for every Json creation path. Json::parse("1") can construct a global Json before a lazily initialized ordinary mutex, making a later destructor unsafe after gate destruction.
The same C++ Json wrapper must not be assigned/moved/destroyed concurrently with use; different live handles may read a shared immutable tree.
standalone_regression_status: Completed: baseline failed all three independent scenarios; candidate passed the identical scenarios.

candidate_code_review.result: No synchronization gap found for the documented shared immutable tree contract.
checked_details: All json-c native calls outside local parsing operate under the same gate.
dump and str construct std::string before the lock_guard is destroyed; keys copies every native key while locked.
at holds lookup plus retain atomically against release; set/push retain and internal release share the gate with destruction.
Type-check helper locks finish before each method takes its own lock; no wrapper-method recursive lock path was found.
Json prvalues from factories/at use guaranteed C++20 copy elision, avoiding an accidental locked copy constructor.
Tokenizers and trees created by parse/ShapeGuard remain thread-private until return, so their native calls cannot access published shared nodes.
A process-lifetime gate avoids use after mutex destruction during global Json teardown.
Move/assignment/is_null still require the documented absence of concurrent mutation/reassignment of the same handle.
